findings.title: Anyone can use up another IP's captcha bucket and lock that user out of wp-login.php
findings.body:
The mint counter is keyed on `get_the_user_ip()`, which trusts X-Forwarded-For by default and takes the right-most entry. On a site that is reached directly, without a trusted proxy, an attacker can call the anonymous `/captcha` REST endpoint 30 times with `X-Forwarded-For: <admin's IP>` and use up that IP's bucket. The same attacker can send a different spoofed IP on every request and never hit the limit.

This bucket is shared with `login_CAPTCHA()`. Once it is full, the login, register and lost-password forms show only a notice and no captcha fields, so `CAPTCHA_CHECK` rejects every login from that IP with "验证码为空" for 10 minutes. Each new burst restarts the 10 minutes. Readers behind a shared NAT who fetch comment captchas while browsing can also block their own logins.

The code relies on site owners turning off XFF trust, but the default stays unsafe. Suggested fixes:
- Rate-limit on `REMOTE_ADDR` unless the site has opted into proxy trust.
- Or keep the login-page mint out of the bucket that the anonymous REST endpoint fills.

held.title: Passwordless/WebAuthn logins now fail because nothing hooks the new skip filter
held.body: The client-side `skip_captcha_check` path is gone, along with the script that hid the captcha when the password field was absent. Now passwordless logins only work if something hooks `sakurairo_skip_login_captcha`, and these hunks add no such hook. If the theme or a plugin a site uses submits `loginform` without a password (passkey/WebAuthn) and sends no `yzm`, or no `cf-turnstile-response` in the Turnstile branch, every such login is now rejected. I could not see whether any built-in passwordless flow exists. If one does, it needs a server-side verified hook on this filter in the same change.
